newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cbank Gov pleased with govt economic package.
newsitem.headline: Czech cbank Gov pleased with govt economic package.

text.p: Czech central bank Governor Josef Tosovsky said on Wednesday he was pleased with the government's package of pro-growth measures, especially limits on public sector wage growth.

Late Wednesday, the government announced sweeping measures aimed at reducing growing budget and trade deficits, while spurring growth, dampening demand for imports and adding confidence to beleaguered capital markets.
But Tosovksy singled out wage growth and public sector spending as two of the key measures he felt were most necessary.

"It certainly is a step in the right direction. I think that the measures concerning wages area and lower budget expenditures were absolutely necessary things," Tosovsky told reporters in reaction to the measures.
The central bank has warned several times the economy would not be able to cope with the inflationary pressures brought about by nominal wage growth of over 10 percent in 1997.
On Wednesday, the government said it was limiting public sector wage growth -- including those for workers at state- owned firms -- to 7.3 percent, down from the originally planned 11.9 percent.
It also cut public sector spending by 25.5 billion crowns, or almost five percent of expected outlays in 1997.
